summary: Pure refactor in packages/cli: nine user-facing literals (help banner, usage lines, unknown-command errors, region prompt, cancel text, db migrate stub warning) move into a new src/messages.ts `as const` object, and prod call sites plus the two pty E2E test files import those constants. Every constant is byte-identical to the literal it replaces and is interpolated in the same position, so CLI output does not change. tsup bundles src/bin/stash.ts, so the new module is inlined into dist/bin/stash.js; it is not exported from the library entry. The one residual risk is a weaker guard: E2E assertions now share the source of truth with prod, so a future edit to messages.ts changes user-visible CLI output without any test failing. AGENTS.md guidance for agents is updated to match. Tests were not run (no node_modules, no CI results).

behaviour_changes.description: Help banner, usage prefixes, unknown command/subcommand errors, region prompt, cancel message and db migrate stub warning are now sourced from src/messages.ts. Values and interpolation are identical to base, so rendered CLI output is unchanged.

E2E tests import the same constants from src/messages.ts instead of hard-coding strings. The db migrate test now asserts on the full warning string rather than the substring 'not yet implemented' (stricter). Assertions no longer independently pin the user-facing wording.
packages/cli/AGENTS.md now tells agents to put test-asserted strings in src/messages.ts and not to hard-code wording in tests. AGENTS.md is not in the package `files` list, so it is not shipped.

failure_scenarios.title: Future copy edits in messages.ts change CLI output with E2E staying green
failure_scenarios.trigger: A later change edits a value in src/messages.ts, e.g. renames 'Unknown command' or 'Cancelled.', on purpose or by accident.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Prod and the E2E assertions read the same constant (messages.ts:12-29; smoke.e2e.test.ts:18-72), so the tests check that the binary prints whatever the constant holds, not that the wording stays stable. At base the tests hard-coded the literals and would fail on such an edit.
failure_scenarios.consequence: User-visible CLI text changes without a failing test. Scripts or docs that match that text could break. CLI stderr text is not a documented contract, so the expected effect is minor and easy to recover from.

existing_verification.description: E2E still verifies that the built binary emits each constant, exit codes, and the user-supplied token, which guards against call-site regressions.

missing_verification: No snapshot or literal assertion pins the user-facing wording itself.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Accept as intended design (documented in AGENTS.md). If wording stability matters, add a small unit snapshot of the `messages` object so wording changes show up in review.

verification_gaps.description: Neither the E2E suite nor the build was run for this assessment, and no CI results were provided. Byte-equivalence of output comes from reading the code, not from execution.

recommended_controls.description: Confirm `pnpm exec turbo run test:e2e --filter @cipherstash/cli` passes in CI for this head. That build-and-run also confirms vitest resolves the `../../src/messages.js` import to the .ts source.
Reviewers of future PRs touching src/messages.ts should treat value edits as user-visible output changes, since tests will not flag them.

evidence.claim: messages object holds the nine strings, each equal to the literal removed at base.
HELP template interpolates versionBannerPrefix + pkg.version and usagePrefix + ' <command> [options]', which yields the same text as base.
Base help text was 'CipherStash CLI v${pkg.version}' and 'Usage: npx @cipherstash/cli <command> [options]'.
migrate warning, unknown db subcommand, and unknown command messages use the constants in the same format strings as base (base lines 195, 198, 259).
Auth usage and 'Unknown auth command: <sub>' are built from constants and match base lines 4 and 47.
selectRegion prompt and cancel message use constants equal to base 'Select a region' / 'Cancelled.'.
Smoke tests import messages from src and assert output contains the constants; migrate test now asserts the full warning.
Cancel test waits for messages.auth.selectRegion and asserts messages.auth.cancelled.
Agent guidance now directs test-asserted strings into src/messages.ts.
Package `files` ships dist, README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG, so AGENTS.md is not published.
The bin entry src/bin/stash.ts is bundled by tsup (skipNodeModulesBundle only externalises node_modules), so relative ../messages.js is inlined.
E2E tests spawn the built dist/bin/stash.js.
CI runs CLI E2E via turbo test:e2e, which depends on build.
At base the E2E assertions hard-coded the literal strings.
